transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Sarah. I just checked my bank account this morning and you've taken two payments of forty-nine pounds on the exact same day! That's nearly a hundred pounds and my rent is due tomorrow!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can pull up your billing ledger on our system. Before I can discuss account transactions, I need to verify your details. Can you give me your postcode and first line of address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 19 St Peter's Grove, York, YO30 6AQ. Please tell me you can reverse one of them immediately because my bank account will be overdrawn.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And what is your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is 8 2 0 4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That verifies the account, thank you Adam. Let me open your invoice schedule now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay. How did two direct debits come out on the same date?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm the billing profile, your account number ends in 4109 and your direct debit mandate is registered with Barclays Bank, is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my Barclays current account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are seeing two payments of forty-nine pounds on the fifteenth of October. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, one was debited at 3 AM and the second one at 6 AM. Why did that happen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me while I check the contract migration log from earlier this month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, I'll wait.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Adam. I can see what happened here. On the second of October, you upgraded your package from Fibre 100 to Fibre 500.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I spoke to an agent who offered me the Fibre 500 upgrade for forty-nine pounds a month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When that change was submitted, your old contract billing cycle was scheduled to close on the fourteenth, while the new Fibre 500 contract created an initial advance bill covering the fifteenth onward.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, but shouldn't the old billing line have cancelled out the duplicate deduction automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously our automated billing gateway should have reconciled the pro-rata balance into a single invoice, but the two collection mandates ran concurrently because the upgrade completed twenty-four hours before the billing cutoff.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So S-Net has taken ninety-eight pounds from my bank instead of forty-nine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the system collected forty-nine pounds for the final cycle of the old Fibre 100 package and forty-nine pounds in advance for the new Fibre 500 package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. I need the duplicate forty-nine pounds refunded back into my bank account today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the direct debit debiting rules on your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you refund it straight to my debit card right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the payment was collected via Direct Debit rather than a debit card transaction, banking regulations mean funds take three business days to clear into our merchant account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean you cannot send it back today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated refund tool cannot issue a same-day card transfer for a Direct Debit payment. What I can do is submit an immediate BACS refund escalation to our billing operations team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long will a BACS refund take to reach my Barclays account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once finance approves the ticket tomorrow morning, the BACS transmission takes two to three banking days, which means the funds will land in your account by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Friday? But my rent goes out tomorrow morning! What am I supposed to do if Barclays charges me an unarranged overdraft fee?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If your bank charges you an overdraft fee as a direct result of this duplicate collection, S-Net will reimburse that fee in full upon receipt of a bank statement showing the charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that helps somewhat, but I would really rather have had the money back today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will submit the BACS refund request for the full forty-nine pounds immediately and apply an urgent processing flag to the ticket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. What happens with my November bill then? Am I going to get billed again on the first?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No. Your regular billing date for the Fibre 500 package is now anchored to the fifteenth of each month. Your next scheduled direct debit will be on the fifteenth of November for forty-nine pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, so there won't be another charge between now and November fifteenth?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There definitely won't be any surprises before the middle of next month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There will definitely be no further charges between now and the fifteenth of November. I have verified that on your active billing schedule.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you give me the reference number for this refund ticket so I have it for my records?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Certainly. The billing operations ticket reference is RFD-88219-YK.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me write that down: R F D 8 8 2 1 9 Y K. Got it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also send an SMS confirmation containing that ticket reference directly to your registered mobile number ending in 204.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would be very helpful, thank you Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Give me one moment while I input the ticket details and apply the credit memo to your ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem, take your time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Adam. The BACS refund ticket has been logged and assigned to the duty finance manager for the morning queue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And you will personally make sure they don't reject it or sit on it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I will track this ticket myself on my personal dashboard and verify when the payment batch clears on Friday morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. I appreciate that you're keeping an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I really hope the bank doesn't penalize me tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As mentioned, if Barclays levies any overdraft or unpaid transaction charge, send us a screenshot of the fee and we will credit it straight to your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. That gives me some peace of mind at least.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me also guide you on how to check your direct debit mandate details in your Barclays app so you can be confident the old collection schedule is gone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, how do I see that on Barclays?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you log into your Barclays mobile app and tap on the Pay & Transfer tab, select Manage Direct Debits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, logging in with Face ID now. Going to Manage Direct Debits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you see S-Net Communications listed there?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, S-Net Communications is listed once, with reference ending in 4109.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms there is only one active mandate registered on your bank account now. The old mandate for the previous package has already been purged by the automated clearing house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a relief to see with my own eyes. I didn't want two mandates lingering in there.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the Direct Debit Guarantee, your bank is also legally bound to refund you immediately if an error is made on an active mandate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I ask Barclays to reverse it today under the Direct Debit Guarantee?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You could invoke the Direct Debit indemnity with Barclays, but since I have already submitted the official BACS refund request RFD-88219-YK on our end, an indemnity claim could cause a duplicate reconciliation hold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, I see. Then I'll leave your refund ticket to run so nothing gets blocked.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is the safest route, and as promised, I am tracking the transaction personally.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a way to set up SMS billing alerts so I get a text three days before each direct debit is taken?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. In the My S-Net portal or app, go to Account Settings and select Notifications.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm in Notifications now. I see Pre-bill Notification.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Toggle on SMS Alert under Pre-bill Notification. Our billing system will then send you an automated text message five days before every payment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just enabled that now. That will prevent any future surprises.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While I have your account open, let me do a quick line sync check on your Fibre 500 connection to make sure there are no packet drops on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead and check that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for about forty seconds while the line tester measures signal attenuation and optical power.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll wait.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Adam. The optical power reading is minus nineteen decibels, which is well within the healthy margin. Your download sync rate is locked at five hundred and twenty megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That sounds really good. My previous Fibre 100 connection was struggling when my flatmate was downloading large video files.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is your Fibre 500 broadband speed working well across all devices at home following the upgrade earlier this month?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the actual internet speed has been great, getting around 480 megabits down. It was just the shock of seeing ninety-eight pounds taken out today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The connection itself is fast and reliable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am glad the broadband performance is meeting expectations, Adam.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, no complaints about the broadband at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also added a ten-pound goodwill credit to your S-Net profile to cover any inconvenience this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, thank you, that is a kind gesture. It will help cover my lunch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has already been applied, so your November bill will automatically reflect thirty-nine pounds instead of forty-nine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant. That definitely softens the blow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your broadband, bills, or account settings that I can check for you today, Adam?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, as long as that forty-nine pounds lands in my account by Friday, that will resolve everything. Thank you Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Adam, and have a good rest of your week.
